name: verify-inkling
description: Drive the inkling Electron desktop app as a user would and prove a feature works. Use when a change touches capture, search, Spaces, note editing, archive or restore, or any user-visible behavior, and you need launch, doctor, drive, evidence, and cleanup on Windows or Linux (Linux runs under Xvfb). Uses CDP against an isolated scratch library; never the real user library.
---

# verify-inkling

Proves inkling behavior by driving the real Electron app over Chrome DevTools Protocol against a scratch data dir. The feature map lives in `features/`; start at `features/README.md` and drive one feature per run.

## Rules

- Use only the scratch library under `<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/<NAME>/library` (override the parent with `INKLING_VERIFY_DIR`). Never point at the developer's real library, never copy from it.
- Stop only the pid this run recorded in `electron.pid` after confirming its cmdline. Never `pkill`, never match processes by name.
- Run one integrated pass per change. Do not run the full suite; CI owns it.
- Linux cannot verify Windows-only behavior (OCR through Windows.Media, WebView2). Report those as unverified.
- Drive through the UI handles below, not internal setters or test-only endpoints.

## Setup

Use the Bun version in `.bun-version`; `bun run check:bun-version` says if it is wrong.

```sh
bun install
bun run build:app      # produces dist/; prints "No demo seed in N built files"
```

## Launch

Same commands on Windows and Linux. Launch starts Electron detached and returns once the app page is listed:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs launch
```

It runs `node_modules/electron/dist/electron .` with `--remote-debugging-port=9333 --user-data-dir=<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/default/library`, writing `electron.pid` and `electron.log` beside the library. On Linux with no `DISPLAY` it wraps Electron in `xvfb-run -a` and adds `--no-sandbox`. Ready means `app://local/index.html` is listed at `http://127.0.0.1:9333/json/list`, which takes about 10 seconds. The first launch against an empty dir shows "0 items in library".

Two instances side by side: give each its own name and port, `INKLING_VERIFY_NAME=b INKLING_VERIFY_PORT=9334 bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs launch`, then pass the same two variables to doctor, drive, and cleanup.

## Doctor

Read-only. Run it first whenever anything looks off:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs doctor
```

Every line must read PASS and the exit code must be 0: pidfile present, pid alive, pid runs our scratch dir, CDP port owned by that pid, app page loaded, library database exists, renderer build present.

## Drive

`scripts/drive.mjs` runs an ordered list of steps against the page and writes evidence. Steps are JSON objects with one key each:

- `click`: CSS selector, clicks the first match.
- `clickText`: `{selector, text}`, clicks the first match whose text contains `text`.
- `fill`: CSS selector plus `text`, focuses and inserts text.
- `key`: `Enter`, `Escape`, or a single character.
- `wait`: selector that must appear.
- `expect`: JavaScript expression that must become true.
- `shot`: PNG filename written into the evidence dir.

Each step may set `label`, and `timeoutMs` (default 8000). A failed step writes `failure.png` and stops the run.

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/drive.mjs 9333 <steps.json> .artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>
```

Selectors come from `src/App.tsx` and `src/features/item-view/`. Prefer the aria-label, title, and class names listed in each feature file over coordinates. Only `features/capture-note.md` has a proven step list; the other feature files are mapped but not yet driven.

## Evidence

Every run writes to `.artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>/` (gitignored):

- `steps.log`: one PASS or FAIL line per step.
- `console.log`: renderer console, exceptions, and log entries captured during the run.
- Numbered screenshots from `shot` steps, plus `failure.png` on a failed step.
- Database proof: read the scratch `library.sqlite3` with bun's `bun:sqlite` in readonly mode, for example `items` rows with `kind`, `body`, `archived`. Include the query output in the run notes.

A proof must show the user action, the visible result, and the stored side effect. A card on screen with no row in `items` is not a pass, and neither is a row with no card.

## Cleanup

Run this after every run, including failed ones:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs cleanup
```

It stops only the recorded pid, then removes that instance's scratch library and pidfile. It confirms the pid's command line names the scratch library first, so a recycled pid is never touched. It never touches `.artifacts/`. Confirm afterwards with `ls .artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>/` that the evidence survived, and that `<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/<NAME>/library` is gone.

## Known platform noise

On Linux, Xvfb has no dbus session, so dbus and dconf errors in `electron.log` are environment noise, not app errors. The sharp Linux warning is also environment-only. Packaged Linux PDF.js worker failure is pre-existing and not caused by this skill.

## Keeping the map current

When a feature's selectors or flow change, update its file in `features/`. `/maintain-verification-skill` is the maintenance loop for keeping this map honest.

# verify-inkling

Proves inkling behavior by driving the real Electron app over Chrome DevTools Protocol against a scratch data dir. The feature map lives in `features/`; start at `features/README.md` and drive one feature per run.

## Rules

- Use only the scratch library under `<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/<NAME>/library` (override the parent with `INKLING_VERIFY_DIR`). Never point at the developer's real library, never copy from it.
- Stop only the pid this run recorded in `electron.pid` after confirming its cmdline. Never `pkill`, never match processes by name.
- Run one integrated pass per change. Do not run the full suite; CI owns it.
- Linux cannot verify Windows-only behavior (OCR through Windows.Media, WebView2). Report those as unverified.
- Drive through the UI handles below, not internal setters or test-only endpoints.

## Setup

Use the Bun version in `.bun-version`; `bun run check:bun-version` says if it is wrong.

```sh
bun install
bun run build:app      # produces dist/; prints "No demo seed in N built files"
```

Bun skips Electron's download script, so a fresh install has no `node_modules/electron/dist`. Run `node node_modules/electron/install.js` once from the repo root before the first launch.

## Launch

Same commands on Windows and Linux. Launch starts Electron detached and returns once the app page is listed:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs launch
```

It runs `node_modules/electron/dist/electron .` with `--remote-debugging-port=9333 --user-data-dir=<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/default/library`, writing `electron.pid` and `electron.log` beside the library. On Linux with no `DISPLAY` it wraps Electron in `xvfb-run -a` and adds `--no-sandbox`. It also passes `--disable-renderer-backgrounding`, `--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows` and `--disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion`: an occluded window reports `visibilityState` "hidden" and stops firing animation frames, which strands the item overlay mid-close and hangs motion-gated steps. Ready means `app://local/index.html` is listed at `http://127.0.0.1:9333/json/list`, which takes about 10 seconds. Launch refuses when the port already has an owner. Other dev servers on the machine often hold 9333, so set `INKLING_VERIFY_PORT` to a free port and pass it to doctor, drive, and cleanup as well. The first launch against an empty dir shows "0 items in library".

Two instances side by side: give each its own name and port, `INKLING_VERIFY_NAME=b INKLING_VERIFY_PORT=9334 bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs launch`, then pass the same two variables to doctor, drive, and cleanup.

## Doctor

Read-only. Run it first whenever anything looks off:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs doctor
```

Every line must read PASS and the exit code must be 0: pidfile present, pid alive, pid runs our scratch dir, CDP port owned by that pid, app page loaded, library database exists, renderer build present.

## Drive

`scripts/drive.mjs` runs an ordered list of steps against the page and writes evidence. Steps are JSON objects with one key each:

- `click`: CSS selector, clicks the first match.
- `clickText`: `{selector, text}`, clicks the first match whose text contains `text`.
- `fill`: CSS selector plus `text`, focuses and inserts text.
- `key`: `Enter`, `Escape`, or a single character.
- `wait`: selector that must appear.
- `expect`: JavaScript expression that must become true.
- `shot`: PNG filename written into the evidence dir.

Each step may set `label`, and `timeoutMs` (default 8000). A failed step writes `failure.png` and stops the run.

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/drive.mjs 9333 <steps.json> .artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>
```

Selectors come from `src/App.tsx` and `src/features/item-view/`. Prefer the aria-label, title, and class names listed in each feature file over coordinates. Only `features/capture-note.md` has a proven step list; the other feature files are mapped but not yet driven.

## Evidence

Every run writes to `.artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>/` (gitignored):

- `steps.log`: one PASS or FAIL line per step.
- `console.log`: renderer console, exceptions, and log entries captured during the run.
- Numbered screenshots from `shot` steps, plus `failure.png` on a failed step.
- Database proof: read the scratch `library.sqlite3` with bun's `bun:sqlite` in readonly mode, for example `items` rows with `kind`, `body`, `archived`. Include the query output in the run notes.

A proof must show the user action, the visible result, and the stored side effect. A card on screen with no row in `items` is not a pass, and neither is a row with no card.

## Cleanup

Run this after every run, including failed ones:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs cleanup
```

It stops only the recorded pid, then removes that instance's scratch library and pidfile. It confirms the pid's command line names the scratch library first, so a recycled pid is never touched. It never touches `.artifacts/`. Confirm afterwards with `ls .artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>/` that the evidence survived, and that `<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/<NAME>/library` is gone.

## Known platform noise

On Linux, Xvfb has no dbus session, so dbus and dconf errors in `electron.log` are environment noise, not app errors. The sharp Linux warning is also environment-only. Packaged Linux PDF.js worker failure is pre-existing and not caused by this skill.

## Keeping the map current

When a feature's selectors or flow change, update its file in `features/`. `/maintain-verification-skill` is the maintenance loop for keeping this map honest.

`scripts/drive.mjs` runs an ordered list of steps against the page and writes evidence. Steps are JSON objects with one key each:

- `click`: CSS selector, clicks the first match.
- `clickText`: `{selector, text}`, clicks the first match whose text contains `text`.
- `fill`: CSS selector plus `text`, focuses, selects the field's text (inputs and textareas only), and inserts text. For a contenteditable, first run an `expect` that calls `getSelection().selectAllChildren(el)`, or `fill` inserts at the caret.
- `key`: `Enter`, `Escape`, or a single character.
- `wait`: selector that must appear.
- `expect`: JavaScript expression that must become true.
- `shot`: PNG filename written into the evidence dir.

Each step may set `label`, and `timeoutMs` (default 8000). `clickText` does not wait; it fails at once if nothing matches yet. A failed step writes `failure.png` and stops the run, and a page that stops answering for 20 seconds fails the step instead of hanging the run.

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/drive.mjs 9333 <steps.json> .artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>
```

## Evidence

Every run writes to `.artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>/` (gitignored):

- `steps.log`: one PASS or FAIL line per step.
- `console.log`: renderer console, exceptions, and log entries captured during the run.
- Numbered screenshots from `shot` steps, plus `failure.png` on a failed step.
- Database proof: read the scratch `library.sqlite3` with bun's `bun:sqlite` in readonly mode, for example `items` rows with `kind`, `body`, `archived`. Include the query output in the run notes.

A proof must show the user action, the visible result, and the stored side effect. A card on screen with no row in `items` is not a pass, and neither is a row with no card.

## Cleanup

Run this after every run, including failed ones:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs cleanup
```

It stops only the recorded pid, then removes that instance's scratch library and pidfile. It confirms the pid's command line names the scratch library first, so a recycled pid is never touched. It never touches `.artifacts/`. Confirm afterwards with `ls .artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>/` that the evidence survived, and that `<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/<NAME>/library` is gone.

On Linux, Xvfb has no dbus session, so dbus and dconf errors in `electron.log` are environment noise, not app errors. The sharp Linux warning is also environment-only. Packaged Linux PDF.js worker failure is pre-existing and not caused by this skill.

# Capture a note from the Add menu

## Sub-features

- Note tile in the Add menu.
- Save to library button, or Enter; the card appears before any processing finishes.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Click Add at the foot of the sidebar. It opens into a menu of Note, Link, Quote, File, and Screen (screenshot). Choose Note, type a line, and press Enter or Save to library. Shift+Enter adds a line break. The new card lands at the top of Everything.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Save as `steps.json`, then run with a fresh evidence dir. Swap the save step for `{"key": "Enter"}` to drive the Enter path; both were driven:

```json
[
  {"label": "open Add", "click": "button[data-tooltip='Add something to your library']"},
  {"label": "choose Note", "clickText": {"selector": ".add-menu-tile", "text": "Note"}},
  {"label": "note field", "wait": "textarea[aria-label='New note']"},
  {"label": "type note", "fill": "textarea[aria-label='New note']", "text": "verify-inkling probe note"},
  {"label": "save", "click": "button.add-menu-save"},
  {"label": "card shows", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article')].some(a => a.textContent.includes('verify-inkling probe note'))", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "dialog closed", "expect": "!document.querySelector('.add-menu-panel')"},
  {"label": "shot", "shot": "note-saved.png"}
]
```

End state proof: the card with the text is in the grid, and `items` has one row with `kind = 'note'`, `title` null, `body = 'verify-inkling probe note'`, `body_format = 'md'`, `description` equal to the body, `metadata = '{"captureSource":"quick note"}'`, `archived = 0`.

## Gotchas

- Note title is null; the text lives in `body`. Check `body`, not `title`. The card shows "Untitled note" with the text in the DOM.
- Add is only clickable while the sidebar is open (the default at 1280 wide). N, pressed outside a text field, opens the sidebar and goes straight to the Note form, skipping the tile menu.
- Text that is only a URL or a bare domain (`example.com`) is saved as a link item, not a note. Keep probe text to words with spaces.
- Link (`input[aria-label='URL to save']`, needs the network) and Quote (`textarea[aria-label='Quote text']`, Enter does not submit) are drivable but not driven here. File and Screen open native pickers and cannot be driven.

# Search your library

## Sub-features

- Text search across notes and titles; "/" focuses the field, Escape clears it.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Press `/` (or Ctrl+K) outside any text field, or click the view pill at the top of the library, and type in the Search your mind field. The grid updates a moment after typing stops. Escape clears the search and restores the grid.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Needs two notes, `alpha probe` and `bravo probe` (see `capture-note.md`). Driven in this order:

```json
[
  {"label": "two cards", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article')].filter(a => /alpha probe|bravo probe/.test(a.textContent)).length === 2"},
  {"label": "slash", "key": "/"},
  {"label": "focused", "expect": "document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-label') === 'Search your mind'"},
  {"label": "type", "fill": "input[aria-label='Search your mind']", "text": "alpha"},
  {"label": "only alpha", "expect": "(() => { const t = [...document.querySelectorAll('article')].map(a => a.textContent); return t.some(x => x.includes('alpha probe')) && !t.some(x => x.includes('bravo probe')); })()", "timeoutMs": 5000},
  {"label": "escape clears", "key": "Escape"},
  {"label": "both back", "expect": "document.querySelectorAll('article').length === 2", "timeoutMs": 5000},
  {"label": "slash", "key": "/"},
  {"label": "no match", "fill": "input[aria-label='Search your mind']", "text": "zzzzqqqq"},
  {"label": "empty state", "expect": "document.body.textContent.includes('Nothing surfaced yet.') && document.querySelectorAll('article').length === 0", "timeoutMs": 5000},
  {"label": "clear", "clickText": {"selector": "button", "text": "Clear search"}},
  {"label": "restored", "expect": "document.querySelectorAll('article').length === 2", "timeoutMs": 5000}
]
```

End state: nothing is stored by a search, so the proof is the visible card set at each step; read `items` once to show both notes were present and `archived = 0`.

## Gotchas

- Matching is whole-token full-text search over title, description, body, OCR text and metadata. `alp` does not match `alpha`; use full words. It works in a scratch library with no embedding model, where it is lexical only.
- Results update about 200 ms after typing stops, so give `expect` a timeout of a few seconds.
- The field is hidden at rest and expands on focus. `/` is ignored while an input has focus; press Escape first.
- The expanded field's hint reads `esc to close`. The result count and the "Save as Space" pill only show while the field is unfocused with a query set; not driven here.

# Spaces

## Sub-features

- Add a Space (Smart or Regular), rename it, delete it. Items are kept when a Space is deleted.
- File an item into a Regular Space from the item overlay.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Click the plus beside Spaces in the sidebar. Name it, choose Smart (the default, stores the current search as its query) or Regular (holds items you file by hand), and press Create Space. The new Space opens at once and a Regular one is empty. To file an item, open it and use Move to Space in the footer; that menu appears only when a Regular Space exists. Rename (pencil) and delete (X) sit on the Space row.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Needs two notes (see `capture-note.md`). Driven in three runs; the Space name field alone does nothing until Create Space is clicked.

```json
[
  {"label": "add Space", "click": "button[aria-label='Add a Space']"},
  {"label": "name field", "wait": "input[aria-label='Space name']"},
  {"label": "name", "fill": "input[aria-label='Space name']", "text": "Verify A"},
  {"label": "Regular", "clickText": {"selector": "label", "text": "Regular"}},
  {"label": "create", "clickText": {"selector": "button[type=submit]", "text": "Create Space"}},
  {"label": "row exists", "wait": "button[aria-label='Rename Verify A']"},
  {"label": "back to Everything", "clickText": {"selector": "button", "text": "Everything"}},
  {"label": "open a card", "expect": "(() => { const a = [...document.querySelectorAll('article.library-card')].find(a => a.textContent.includes('bravo probe')); if (!a) return false; a.click(); return true; })()"},
  {"label": "overlay", "wait": "section[role='dialog'] button[aria-label='Close details']"},
  {"label": "Move to Space", "click": "button[aria-label='Move to Space']"},
  {"label": "file it", "clickText": {"selector": "[role='menuitemcheckbox']", "text": "Verify A"}},
  {"label": "close menu", "key": "Escape"},
  {"label": "close overlay", "click": "button[aria-label='Close details']"},
  {"label": "rename", "click": "button[aria-label='Rename Verify A']"},
  {"label": "rename input", "wait": "input[aria-label='Rename Verify A']"},
  {"label": "new name", "fill": "input[aria-label='Rename Verify A']", "text": "Verify B"},
  {"label": "commit", "key": "Enter"},
  {"label": "renamed", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('button[aria-pressed]')].some(b => b.textContent.includes('Verify B'))"},
  {"label": "delete", "click": "button[aria-label='Delete Verify B']"},
  {"label": "gone", "expect": "![...document.querySelectorAll('button[aria-pressed]')].some(b => b.textContent.includes('Verify'))"},
  {"label": "items kept", "expect": "document.querySelectorAll('article').length === 2", "timeoutMs": 5000}
]
```

Split the file after "create" and after "close overlay" to read the database between runs. End state, read from `library.sqlite3` readonly: after create, `spaces` has one row with `kind = 'regular'` and `query = '{}'`; after filing, `space_items` has one row linking the Space `id` to the item id; after delete, `spaces` and `space_items` are empty and both `items` rows still have `archived = 0`.

## Gotchas

- Everything and Space rows are different: a Space row is `button[aria-pressed]`, the Everything row has no `aria-pressed`, so select it with `clickText` on `button`.
- Rename and delete are hover-revealed but `click` works on them without hovering. There is no delete confirmation. Delete is `button[aria-label='Delete <name>']`; `data-tooltip='Delete Space'` matches the first row only.
- `Rename <name>` is both the pencil button's and the input's `aria-label`; prefix the selector with `button` or `input`.
- A Smart Space cannot hold hand-filed items, so Move to Space lists Regular Spaces only. A Smart Space made while the search box has text takes that text as its query.

# Edit a note

## Sub-features

- Open a note in the item overlay, choose Edit note, save, close.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Click a note card to open it in the overlay. On the Info tab, choose Edit note, change the text in the editor, and press Save note. Saving returns to the Info tab with the overlay still open. Cancel, Close, and Escape discard the edit and only leave the editor; close the overlay afterwards with Close or Escape.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Needs a note whose text is `alpha probe` (see `capture-note.md`). Record its `updated_at` first.

```json
[
  {"label": "open card", "expect": "(() => { const a = [...document.querySelectorAll('article.library-card')].find(a => a.textContent.includes('alpha probe')); if (!a) return false; a.click(); return true; })()", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "overlay open", "wait": "section[role='dialog'] button[aria-label='Close details']"},
  {"label": "Edit note", "clickText": {"selector": "button", "text": "Edit note"}},
  {"label": "editor shown", "wait": "div[aria-label='Note content']"},
  {"label": "body loaded", "expect": "document.querySelector(\"div[aria-label='Note content']\").textContent.includes('alpha probe')", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "select all", "expect": "(() => { const e = document.querySelector(\"div[aria-label='Note content']\"); e.focus(); document.getSelection().selectAllChildren(e); return true; })()"},
  {"label": "replace text", "fill": "div[aria-label='Note content']", "text": "alpha edited"},
  {"label": "typed", "expect": "document.querySelector(\"div[aria-label='Note content']\").textContent.trim() === 'alpha edited'"},
  {"label": "Save", "click": "button[aria-label='Save note']"},
  {"label": "editor gone", "expect": "!document.querySelector(\"div[aria-label='Note content']\")", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "close overlay", "click": "button[aria-label='Close details']"},
  {"label": "overlay closed", "expect": "!document.querySelector(\"button[aria-label='Close details']\")", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "card shows new text", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article.library-card')].some(a => a.textContent.includes('alpha edited'))", "timeoutMs": 10000}
]
```

End state: the `items` row has `body = 'alpha edited'`, `description` the same, `body_format = 'md'`, `title` still null, `created_at` unchanged and `updated_at` moved forward.

## Gotchas

- The editor is a rich-text contenteditable (`div[aria-label='Note content']`), not a textarea, so `fill` needs the select-all step first or it inserts at the caret.
- Edit note is a plain button with no `aria-label`; find it with `clickText`. It lives in the Info tab, not a toolbar.
- The Close button reads "Close details", or "Close editor" while editing. There is no autosave and an empty note is refused.
- Closing animates, so it needs a visible window (see the occlusion note in `SKILL.md`).

# Archive and restore

## Sub-features

- Archive an item from the overlay; restore it from the archive panel, one tile or a selected batch.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Open an item and press Archive in the footer (right-clicking a card also offers Archive). The card leaves Everything and a "Forgotten from your library" toast offers Undo. Archived items appear in Settings, under the Archive tab. Restore on a tile returns one item; Select, picking tiles, then Restore returns a batch.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Needs a note whose text is `bravo probe` (see `capture-note.md`). Driven as one run; for the batch path, replace the "restore tile" and "tile gone" steps with the batch steps below.

```json
[
  {"label": "open card", "expect": "(() => { const a = [...document.querySelectorAll('article.library-card')].find(a => a.textContent.includes('bravo probe')); if (!a) return false; a.click(); return true; })()"},
  {"label": "footer Archive", "wait": "section[role='dialog'] footer button[aria-label='Archive']"},
  {"label": "archive", "click": "button[aria-label='Archive']"},
  {"label": "card leaves", "expect": "![...document.querySelectorAll('article')].some(a => a.textContent.includes('bravo probe'))", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "toast", "expect": "document.body.textContent.includes('Forgotten from your library')", "timeoutMs": 5000},
  {"label": "open Settings", "click": "button[aria-label='Settings']"},
  {"label": "settings modal", "wait": "#settings-modal"},
  {"label": "Archive tab", "clickText": {"selector": "[role='tab']", "text": "Archive"}},
  {"label": "tile present", "wait": "#settings-modal article[data-library-item-id]"},
  {"label": "restore tile", "click": "#settings-modal article[data-library-item-id] button[data-tooltip='Restore to library']"},
  {"label": "tile gone", "expect": "!document.querySelector('#settings-modal article[data-library-item-id]')", "timeoutMs": 8000},
  {"label": "empty state", "expect": "document.querySelector('#settings-modal').textContent.includes('Your archive is empty')"},
  {"label": "close settings", "key": "Escape"},
  {"label": "card returns", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article')].some(a => a.textContent.includes('bravo probe'))", "timeoutMs": 8000}
]
```

Batch path, in place of "restore tile" and "tile gone":

```json
[
  {"label": "Select mode", "click": "button[aria-label='Select archived items']"},
  {"label": "select tile", "click": "#settings-modal article[data-library-item-id]"},
  {"label": "1 selected", "expect": "document.querySelector('#settings-modal').textContent.includes('1 selected')"},
  {"label": "batch Restore", "clickText": {"selector": "fieldset button", "text": "Restore"}},
  {"label": "tile gone", "expect": "!document.querySelector('#settings-modal article[data-library-item-id]')", "timeoutMs": 8000}
]
```

End state: after archive, the `items` row has `archived = 1` and `updated_at` moved; after restore it is `archived = 0` and the card is back in Everything.

## Gotchas

- Archive is a soft flag in `items.archived` (no `archived_at`), and there is no Trash. Delete forever is separate: it works only on archived items, after a 10 second Undo window, and also removes `assets/items/<id>/`. Not driven here.
- The tile Restore button has no `aria-label` and is invisible until hover, but `click` works on it. In selection mode the tile buttons disappear and only the header Restore remains, disabled until a tile is selected.
- The Archive tab label carries a count, so match it with `clickText`, not equality.
- Archiving animates the overlay away, so it needs a visible window (see the occlusion note in `SKILL.md`).

# Capture a note from the Add menu

## Sub-features

- Note tile in the Add menu.
- Save to library button, or Enter; the card appears before any processing finishes.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Click Add at the foot of the sidebar. It opens into a menu of Note, Link, Quote, File, and Screen (screenshot). Choose Note, type a line, and press Enter or Save to library. Shift+Enter adds a line break. The new card lands at the top of Everything.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Save as `steps.json`, then run with a fresh evidence dir. Swap the save step for `{"key": "Enter"}` to drive the Enter path; both were driven:

```json
[
  {"label": "open Add", "click": "button[data-tooltip='Add something to your library']"},
  {"label": "choose Note", "clickText": {"selector": ".add-menu-tile", "text": "Note"}},
  {"label": "note field", "wait": "textarea[aria-label='New note']"},
  {"label": "type note", "fill": "textarea[aria-label='New note']", "text": "verify-inkling probe note"},
  {"label": "save", "click": "button.add-menu-save"},
  {"label": "card shows", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article')].some(a => a.textContent.includes('verify-inkling probe note'))", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "dialog closed", "expect": "!document.querySelector('.add-menu-panel')"},
  {"label": "shot", "shot": "note-saved.png"}
]
```

End state proof: the card with the text is in the grid, and `items` has one row with `kind = 'note'`, `title` null, `body = 'verify-inkling probe note'`, `body_format = 'md'`, `description` equal to the body, `metadata = '{"captureSource":"quick note"}'`, `archived = 0`.

## Gotchas

- Note title is null; the text lives in `body`. Check `body`, not `title`. The card shows "Untitled note" with the text in the DOM.
- Add is only clickable while the sidebar is open (the default at 1280 wide). N, pressed outside a text field, opens the sidebar and goes straight to the Note form, skipping the tile menu.
- Text that is only a URL or a bare domain (`example.com`) is saved as a link item, not a note. Keep probe text to words with spaces.
- Link (`input[aria-label='URL to save']`, needs the network) and Quote (`textarea[aria-label='Quote text']`, Enter does not submit) are drivable but not driven here. File and Screen open native pickers and cannot be driven.

# Search your library

## Sub-features

- Text search across notes and titles; "/" focuses the field, Escape clears it.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Press `/` (or Ctrl+K) outside any text field, or click the view pill at the top of the library, and type in the Search your mind field. The grid updates a moment after typing stops. Escape clears the search and restores the grid.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Needs two notes, `alpha probe` and `bravo probe` (see `capture-note.md`). Driven in this order:

```json
[
  {"label": "two cards", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article')].filter(a => /alpha probe|bravo probe/.test(a.textContent)).length === 2"},
  {"label": "slash", "key": "/"},
  {"label": "focused", "expect": "document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-label') === 'Search your mind'"},
  {"label": "type", "fill": "input[aria-label='Search your mind']", "text": "alpha"},
  {"label": "only alpha", "expect": "(() => { const t = [...document.querySelectorAll('article')].map(a => a.textContent); return t.some(x => x.includes('alpha probe')) && !t.some(x => x.includes('bravo probe')); })()", "timeoutMs": 5000},
  {"label": "escape clears", "key": "Escape"},
  {"label": "both back", "expect": "document.querySelectorAll('article').length === 2", "timeoutMs": 5000},
  {"label": "slash", "key": "/"},
  {"label": "no match", "fill": "input[aria-label='Search your mind']", "text": "zzzzqqqq"},
  {"label": "empty state", "expect": "document.body.textContent.includes('Nothing surfaced yet.') && document.querySelectorAll('article').length === 0", "timeoutMs": 5000},
  {"label": "clear", "clickText": {"selector": "button", "text": "Clear search"}},
  {"label": "restored", "expect": "document.querySelectorAll('article').length === 2", "timeoutMs": 5000}
]
```

End state: nothing is stored by a search, so the proof is the visible card set at each step; read `items` once to show both notes were present and `archived = 0`.

## Gotchas

- Matching is whole-token full-text search over title, description, body, OCR text and metadata. `alp` does not match `alpha`; use full words. It works in a scratch library with no embedding model, where it is lexical only.
- Results update about 200 ms after typing stops, so give `expect` a timeout of a few seconds.
- The field is hidden at rest and expands on focus. `/` is ignored while an input has focus; press Escape first.
- The expanded field's hint reads `esc to close`. The result count and the "Save as Space" pill only show while the field is unfocused with a query set; not driven here.

# Spaces

## Sub-features

- Add a Space (Smart or Regular), rename it, delete it. Items are kept when a Space is deleted.
- File an item into a Regular Space from the item overlay.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Click the plus beside Spaces in the sidebar. Name it, choose Smart (the default, stores the current search as its query) or Regular (holds items you file by hand), and press Create Space. The new Space opens at once and a Regular one is empty. To file an item, open it and use Move to Space in the footer; that menu appears only when a Regular Space exists. Rename (pencil) and delete (X) sit on the Space row.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Needs two notes (see `capture-note.md`). Driven in three runs; the Space name field alone does nothing until Create Space is clicked.

```json
[
  {"label": "add Space", "click": "button[aria-label='Add a Space']"},
  {"label": "name field", "wait": "input[aria-label='Space name']"},
  {"label": "name", "fill": "input[aria-label='Space name']", "text": "Verify A"},
  {"label": "Regular", "clickText": {"selector": "label", "text": "Regular"}},
  {"label": "create", "clickText": {"selector": "button[type=submit]", "text": "Create Space"}},
  {"label": "row exists", "wait": "button[aria-label='Rename Verify A']"},
  {"label": "back to Everything", "clickText": {"selector": "button", "text": "Everything"}},
  {"label": "open a card", "expect": "(() => { const a = [...document.querySelectorAll('article.library-card')].find(a => a.textContent.includes('bravo probe')); if (!a) return false; a.click(); return true; })()"},
  {"label": "overlay", "wait": "section[role='dialog'] button[aria-label='Close details']"},
  {"label": "Move to Space", "click": "button[aria-label='Move to Space']"},
  {"label": "file it", "clickText": {"selector": "[role='menuitemcheckbox']", "text": "Verify A"}},
  {"label": "close menu", "key": "Escape"},
  {"label": "close overlay", "click": "button[aria-label='Close details']"},
  {"label": "rename", "click": "button[aria-label='Rename Verify A']"},
  {"label": "rename input", "wait": "input[aria-label='Rename Verify A']"},
  {"label": "new name", "fill": "input[aria-label='Rename Verify A']", "text": "Verify B"},
  {"label": "commit", "key": "Enter"},
  {"label": "renamed", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('button[aria-pressed]')].some(b => b.textContent.includes('Verify B'))"},
  {"label": "delete", "click": "button[aria-label='Delete Verify B']"},
  {"label": "gone", "expect": "![...document.querySelectorAll('button[aria-pressed]')].some(b => b.textContent.includes('Verify'))"},
  {"label": "items kept", "expect": "document.querySelectorAll('article').length === 2", "timeoutMs": 5000}
]
```

Split the file after "create" and after "close overlay" to read the database between runs. End state, read from `library.sqlite3` readonly: after create, `spaces` has one row with `kind = 'regular'` and `query = '{}'`; after filing, `space_items` has one row linking the Space `id` to the item id; after delete, `spaces` and `space_items` are empty and both `items` rows still have `archived = 0`.

## Gotchas

- Everything and Space rows are different: a Space row is `button[aria-pressed]`, the Everything row has no `aria-pressed`, so select it with `clickText` on `button`.
- Rename and delete are hover-revealed but `click` works on them without hovering. There is no delete confirmation. Delete is `button[aria-label='Delete <name>']`; `data-tooltip='Delete Space'` matches the first row only.
- `Rename <name>` is both the pencil button's and the input's `aria-label`; prefix the selector with `button` or `input`.
- A Smart Space cannot hold hand-filed items, so Move to Space lists Regular Spaces only. A Smart Space made while the search box has text takes that text as its query.

# Edit a note

## Sub-features

- Open a note in the item overlay, choose Edit note, save, close.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Click a note card to open it in the overlay. On the Info tab, choose Edit note, change the text in the editor, and press Save note. Saving returns to the Info tab with the overlay still open. Cancel, Close, and Escape discard the edit and only leave the editor; close the overlay afterwards with Close or Escape.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Needs a note whose text is `alpha probe` (see `capture-note.md`). Record its `updated_at` first.

```json
[
  {"label": "open card", "expect": "(() => { const a = [...document.querySelectorAll('article.library-card')].find(a => a.textContent.includes('alpha probe')); if (!a) return false; a.click(); return true; })()", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "overlay open", "wait": "section[role='dialog'] button[aria-label='Close details']"},
  {"label": "Edit note", "clickText": {"selector": "button", "text": "Edit note"}},
  {"label": "editor shown", "wait": "div[aria-label='Note content']"},
  {"label": "body loaded", "expect": "document.querySelector(\"div[aria-label='Note content']\").textContent.includes('alpha probe')", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "select all", "expect": "(() => { const e = document.querySelector(\"div[aria-label='Note content']\"); e.focus(); document.getSelection().selectAllChildren(e); return true; })()"},
  {"label": "replace text", "fill": "div[aria-label='Note content']", "text": "alpha edited"},
  {"label": "typed", "expect": "document.querySelector(\"div[aria-label='Note content']\").textContent.trim() === 'alpha edited'"},
  {"label": "Save", "click": "button[aria-label='Save note']"},
  {"label": "editor gone", "expect": "!document.querySelector(\"div[aria-label='Note content']\")", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "close overlay", "click": "button[aria-label='Close details']"},
  {"label": "overlay closed", "expect": "!document.querySelector(\"button[aria-label='Close details']\")", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "card shows new text", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article.library-card')].some(a => a.textContent.includes('alpha edited'))", "timeoutMs": 10000}
]
```

## Gotchas

- The editor is a rich-text contenteditable (`div[aria-label='Note content']`), not a textarea, so `fill` needs the select-all step first or it inserts at the caret.
- Edit note is a plain button with no `aria-label`; find it with `clickText`. It lives in the Info tab, not a toolbar.
- The Close button reads "Close details", or "Close editor" while editing. There is no autosave and an empty note is refused.
- Closing animates, so it needs a visible window (see the occlusion note in `SKILL.md`).

# Archive and restore

## Sub-features

- Archive an item from the overlay; restore it from the archive panel, one tile or a selected batch.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Open an item and press Archive in the footer (right-clicking a card also offers Archive). The card leaves Everything and a "Forgotten from your library" toast offers Undo. Archived items appear in Settings, under the Archive tab. Restore on a tile returns one item; Select, picking tiles, then Restore returns a batch.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Needs a note whose text is `bravo probe` (see `capture-note.md`). Driven as one run; for the batch path, replace the "restore tile" and "tile gone" steps with the batch steps below.

```json
[
  {"label": "open card", "expect": "(() => { const a = [...document.querySelectorAll('article.library-card')].find(a => a.textContent.includes('bravo probe')); if (!a) return false; a.click(); return true; })()"},
  {"label": "footer Archive", "wait": "section[role='dialog'] footer button[aria-label='Archive']"},
  {"label": "archive", "click": "button[aria-label='Archive']"},
  {"label": "card leaves", "expect": "![...document.querySelectorAll('article')].some(a => a.textContent.includes('bravo probe'))", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "toast", "expect": "document.body.textContent.includes('Forgotten from your library')", "timeoutMs": 5000},
  {"label": "open Settings", "click": "button[aria-label='Settings']"},
  {"label": "settings modal", "wait": "#settings-modal"},
  {"label": "Archive tab", "clickText": {"selector": "[role='tab']", "text": "Archive"}},
  {"label": "tile present", "wait": "#settings-modal article[data-library-item-id]"},
  {"label": "restore tile", "click": "#settings-modal article[data-library-item-id] button[data-tooltip='Restore to library']"},
  {"label": "tile gone", "expect": "!document.querySelector('#settings-modal article[data-library-item-id]')", "timeoutMs": 8000},
  {"label": "empty state", "expect": "document.querySelector('#settings-modal').textContent.includes('Your archive is empty')"},
  {"label": "close settings", "key": "Escape"},
  {"label": "card returns", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article')].some(a => a.textContent.includes('bravo probe'))", "timeoutMs": 8000}
]
```

Batch path, in place of "restore tile" and "tile gone":

```json
[
  {"label": "Select mode", "click": "button[aria-label='Select archived items']"},
  {"label": "select tile", "click": "#settings-modal article[data-library-item-id]"},
  {"label": "1 selected", "expect": "document.querySelector('#settings-modal').textContent.includes('1 selected')"},
  {"label": "batch Restore", "clickText": {"selector": "fieldset button", "text": "Restore"}},
  {"label": "tile gone", "expect": "!document.querySelector('#settings-modal article[data-library-item-id]')", "timeoutMs": 8000}
]
```

End state: after archive, the `items` row has `archived = 1` and `updated_at` moved; after restore it is `archived = 0` and the card is back in Everything.

## Gotchas

- Archive is a soft flag in `items.archived` (no `archived_at`), and there is no Trash. Delete forever is separate: it works only on archived items, after a 10 second Undo window, and also removes `assets/items/<id>/`. Not driven here.
- The tile Restore button has no `aria-label` and is invisible until hover, but `click` works on it. In selection mode the tile buttons disappear and only the header Restore remains, disabled until a tile is selected.
- The Archive tab label carries a count, so match it with `clickText`, not equality.
- Archiving animates the overlay away, so it needs a visible window (see the occlusion note in `SKILL.md`).

# Search your library

## Sub-features

- Text search across notes and titles; "/" focuses the field, Escape clears it.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Press `/` (or Ctrl+K) outside any text field, or click the view pill at the top of the library, and type in the Search your mind field. The grid updates a moment after typing stops. Escape clears the search and restores the grid.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Needs two notes, `alpha probe` and `bravo probe` (see `capture-note.md`). Driven in this order:

```json
[
  {"label": "two cards", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article')].filter(a => /alpha probe|bravo probe/.test(a.textContent)).length === 2"},
  {"label": "slash", "key": "/"},
  {"label": "focused", "expect": "document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-label') === 'Search your mind'"},
  {"label": "type", "fill": "input[aria-label='Search your mind']", "text": "alpha"},
  {"label": "only alpha", "expect": "(() => { const t = [...document.querySelectorAll('article')].map(a => a.textContent); return t.some(x => x.includes('alpha probe')) && !t.some(x => x.includes('bravo probe')); })()", "timeoutMs": 5000},
  {"label": "escape clears", "key": "Escape"},
  {"label": "both back", "expect": "document.querySelectorAll('article').length === 2", "timeoutMs": 5000},
  {"label": "slash", "key": "/"},
  {"label": "no match", "fill": "input[aria-label='Search your mind']", "text": "zzzzqqqq"},
  {"label": "empty state", "expect": "document.body.textContent.includes('Nothing surfaced yet.') && document.querySelectorAll('article').length === 0", "timeoutMs": 5000},
  {"label": "clear", "clickText": {"selector": "button", "text": "Clear search"}},
  {"label": "restored", "expect": "document.querySelectorAll('article').length === 2", "timeoutMs": 5000}
]
```

End state: nothing is stored by a search, so the proof is the visible card set at each step; read `items` once to show both notes were present and `archived = 0`.

## Gotchas

- Matching is whole-token full-text search over title, description, body, OCR text and metadata. `alp` does not match `alpha`; use full words. It works in a scratch library with no embedding model, where it is lexical only.
- Results update about 200 ms after typing stops, so give `expect` a timeout of a few seconds.
- The field is hidden at rest and expands on focus. `/` is ignored while an input has focus; press Escape first.
- The expanded field's hint reads `esc to close`. The result count and the "Save as Space" pill only show while the field is unfocused with a query set; not driven here.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__delegate_task
tools.description: Start one child agent with only `task`. No parent history. Separate checkout or PR per child: `isolation:'worktree'`. Keep `taskId` for `task_status` and `task_cancel`.

options.description: Options from `orchestrator_capabilities`, such as {effort:'max'}. Given values override inherited. [] or {} clears.

isolation.description: 'shared' (default): parent checkout. 'worktree': new prepared checkout from the parent commit, for a separate checkout or PR per child. Uncommitted edits stay out.

mode.description: Default 'async'. 'wait' only if this turn needs the result. A question or approval ends the wait.

timeoutMs.description: Mode 'wait' only. Default 10 min. A timeout does not cancel the child.

runtimeMode.description: Omit unless the user asks for a supervised child. Narrow modes pause for human approval, not read-only. Above yours is rejected.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__link_pull_request
tools.description: Link a PR to this thread. T3 shows its status and settles the thread on merge.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__orchestrator_capabilities
tools.description: List providers, models, options, and runtime modes for `delegate_task`. Short list. `search` finds others. Any catalog model works.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_background_wait
tools.description: Keep this thread in Working while background work runs. Pass its task ID after starting it. Not for work left running (dev server, watcher). `waiting=false` clears. Does not stop the task. Claude only.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__task_cancel
tools.description: Stop one delegated task by `taskId`. Stops its running and queued turns, its delegates, and its PR watches, including later runs in its child thread. A finished task keeps its result.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__task_status
tools.description: Read one delegated task you started. Do not call it on a running task before its completion wakes you. `workState`: working, waiting_for_children, result_available. A finished turn with live child work is not done. `summary`: final result. Reading it marks it delivered.

content.text:
Partly. Each gap is a different case.

- **Search count and "Save as Space" pill: yes.** Both are user-facing search UI and need no network. The pill is also the route into Smart Spaces from a search, so it ties search and Spaces together. I'd add them to `search.md` and drive them once. Both only show while the field is unfocused with a query set, so the steps would run Escape first and then assert `.result-count` and the pill.
- **`spaces` rows after rename: yes, but it's a run gap, not a skill gap.** `spaces.md` already says to split the run and read the database between steps. I just didn't read it after the rename. The fix is one extra read of `name` and `updated_at`.
- **Quote capture: yes, I'd add it.** The Quote tile (`textarea[aria-label='Quote text']`) works offline and is a capture path the map has no entry for. I'd write a `capture-quote.md`. Enter doesn't submit there, so the steps click `button.add-menu-save`.
- **Link capture: only as a documented limit.** Saving a URL fetches it over the network, so a run would depend on external state. If you want it covered, it needs a URL the run can reach reliably. A local fixture server would be machine-specific state, which this repo avoids.
- **File and Screen: documented limit only.** Both open native pickers or the OS screenshot flow, and `drive.mjs` only talks to the page over CDP. The skill already lists them as undrivable with that reason in the capture-note gotchas. If it should be more explicit, I'd add them to `features/README.md` the way deep-link capture is listed.

I haven't changed anything for these. If you want the first three, I'd add them to PR #202 and re-drive them, since a doc step that wasn't run shouldn't ship. Should I?

# Capture a quote from the Add menu

## Sub-features

- Quote tile in the Add menu, with optional attribution and source URL.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Click Add at the foot of the sidebar and choose Quote. Type the quote, optionally add who said it and a source link, and press Save to library. The new card lands at the top of Everything.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

```json
[
  {"label": "open Add", "click": "button[data-tooltip='Add something to your library']"},
  {"label": "choose Quote", "clickText": {"selector": ".add-menu-tile", "text": "Quote"}},
  {"label": "quote field", "wait": "textarea[aria-label='Quote text']"},
  {"label": "type quote", "fill": "textarea[aria-label='Quote text']", "text": "verify quote text"},
  {"label": "attribution", "fill": "input[aria-label='Quote attribution']", "text": "Ada Probe, Notes"},
  {"label": "save", "click": "button.add-menu-save"},
  {"label": "card shows", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article')].some(a => a.textContent.includes('verify quote text'))", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "dialog closed", "expect": "!document.querySelector('.add-menu-panel')"},
  {"label": "shot", "shot": "quote-saved.png"}
]
```

End state: the card is in the grid, and `items` has one row with `kind = 'quote'`, `title = 'verify quote text'`, `description = 'Ada Probe, Notes'`, `body = ''`, `source_label = 'Ada Probe'`, `archived = 0`, and `metadata.quoteText` equal to the quote.

## Gotchas

- The quote text is stored in `title` and the attribution in `description`, the reverse of a note, which keeps its text in `body`.
- Leave the source URL empty. A URL is normalised and becomes the `source_label` host, and the quote can then depend on external state.
- Same Add-menu rules as `capture-note.md`: the sidebar must be open.

# Capture a note from the Add menu

## Sub-features

- Note tile in the Add menu.
- Save to library button, or Enter; the card appears before any processing finishes.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Click Add at the foot of the sidebar. It opens into a menu of Note, Link, Quote, File, and Screen (screenshot). Choose Note, type a line, and press Enter or Save to library. Shift+Enter adds a line break. The new card lands at the top of Everything.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Save as `steps.json`, then run with a fresh evidence dir. Swap the save step for `{"key": "Enter"}` to drive the Enter path; both were driven:

```json
[
  {"label": "open Add", "click": "button[data-tooltip='Add something to your library']"},
  {"label": "choose Note", "clickText": {"selector": ".add-menu-tile", "text": "Note"}},
  {"label": "note field", "wait": "textarea[aria-label='New note']"},
  {"label": "type note", "fill": "textarea[aria-label='New note']", "text": "verify-inkling probe note"},
  {"label": "save", "click": "button.add-menu-save"},
  {"label": "card shows", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article')].some(a => a.textContent.includes('verify-inkling probe note'))", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "dialog closed", "expect": "!document.querySelector('.add-menu-panel')"},
  {"label": "shot", "shot": "note-saved.png"}
]
```

End state proof: the card with the text is in the grid, and `items` has one row with `kind = 'note'`, `title` null, `body = 'verify-inkling probe note'`, `body_format = 'md'`, `description` equal to the body, `metadata = '{"captureSource":"quick note"}'`, `archived = 0`.

## Gotchas

- Note title is null; the text lives in `body`. Check `body`, not `title`. The card shows "Untitled note" with the text in the DOM.
- Add is only clickable while the sidebar is open (the default at 1280 wide). N, pressed outside a text field, opens the sidebar and goes straight to the Note form, skipping the tile menu.
- Text that is only a URL or a bare domain (`example.com`) is saved as a link item, not a note. Keep probe text to words with spaces.
- Link (`input[aria-label='URL to save']`, needs the network) and Quote (`textarea[aria-label='Quote text']`, Enter does not submit) are drivable but not driven here. File and Screen open native pickers and cannot be driven.
